_readme: Curated 'Around Boston' links for the home page. Takeaways are written in our own words, never copied. Check each URL still loads before publishing. Last checked 2026-11-17.

items.title: Household Employer's Tax Guide (Pub. 926), 2026
items.takeaway: Pay one household employee $3,000 or more in 2026 and you owe Social Security and Medicare on all of it, not just the amount over $3,000.

items.title: Domestic workers: notice of rights and model agreement
items.takeaway: Once a nanny works 16 or more hours a week, Massachusetts requires a signed written agreement before work starts. The AG's office offers a free model you can fill in.

items.title: PFML contribution rates and calculator
items.takeaway: A household with one employee sends 0.46% of wages for paid leave, and all of it can come out of the nanny's paycheck. There's no employer share under 25 employees.

items.title: National Database of Childcare Prices
items.takeaway: Daycare prices for every county, including Suffolk, Middlesex and Norfolk. The newest data is from 2022, so expect today's prices to be higher.

items.title: 2026 Salary & Benefits Guide
items.takeaway: A Boston agency's view of what household staff are paid, including the benefits families usually offer.
